question: Three agents discuss binary search on sorted arrays. Which position is best supported?
options: Binary search checks every element before deciding.
Binary search needs extra memory proportional to the array.
Binary search finds a target in logarithmic time on sorted arrays.
Binary search works on unsorted arrays.
gold_answer: Binary search finds a target in logarithmic time on sorted arrays.
notes: Team-authored original item on binary search on sorted arrays. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Binary search needs extra memory proportional to the array.

claims.text: Binary search runs in logarithmic time.

evidence.text: Halving n elements down to one takes a number of steps proportional to log n.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage counts halving steps as logarithmic, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Binary search is faster than constant-time dictionary lookup.

evidence.text: Hash lookups average constant time, which beats the logarithmic steps of binary search.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage ranks constant time above logarithmic steps, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Sorting is never worthwhile before searching.

evidence.text: Total times were compared with and without a sorting pass for repeated queries.

claims.verdict_rationale: One comparison cannot show sorting is never worthwhile, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Binary search works on unsorted arrays.

claims.text: Binary search halves the remaining range with each comparison.

evidence.text: Each comparison discards the half that cannot contain the target, halving the search interval.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes halving the interval per comparison, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Binary search examines the middle element last.

evidence.text: The algorithm examines the middle element first at every stage, not last.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the middle comes first, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Step counts were measured for several logarithmic procedures.

claims.verdict_rationale: Measuring counts cannot show all are identical, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Binary search finds a target in logarithmic time on sorted arrays.

claims.text: Binary search requires the array to be sorted.

evidence.text: Discarding a half is valid only when ordering guarantees the target's side, which sorting provides.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage makes sorting the guarantee for discarding, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Binary search works by scanning from both ends inward.

evidence.text: Scanning from both ends is a different technique; binary search repeatedly probes the midpoint.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage identifies midpoint probing, not end scanning, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Binary search is the fastest possible algorithm for every problem.

evidence.text: Running times were benchmarked for binary search on one lookup task.

claims.verdict_rationale: One benchmark cannot show universal optimality, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
